universities.name: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.location: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden
universities.desc: KTH offers a two-year MSc in Vehicle Engineering, taught in English. Students can specialise in road or rail vehicles. The road-vehicle pathway is particularly relevant to students interested in cars, trucks, buses, vehicle dynamics, design, electrification and safety systems. **Location:** Stockholm, Sweden **![][image1]**

universities.name: \. Chalmers University of Technology
universities.desc: Chalmers offers an MSc in Mobility Engineering with a specialisation in Automotive Engineering. Students can explore vehicle dynamics and control, powertrains, traffic safety, aerodynamics, electric and hybrid vehicles, and propulsion technologies. The optional Formula Student project can provide practical experience in vehicle development and engineering. **Location:** Gothenburg, Sweden **![][image2]** **Which university should you choose?** KTH offers a broader vehicle engineering education, with opportunities to focus on road or rail vehicles. Chalmers is a relevant choice for students who want to specialise in automotive engineering through its Mobility Engineering programme. Compare the curriculum, eligibility criteria and project options before making a decision.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Automobile Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Automobile Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Automobile Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
